items.note: Dēvapāla's Harsaudā record: temple of Śambhu built by merchant Kēśava, a resident of Undapura, with a tank and images including Nakulīśa and Ambikā.
Earliest known record linking Dēvapāla of the Mahākumāra line to the main Paramāra house at Dhāra; he apparently succeeded Arjunavarman before 1218 A.C.
In the two inscriptions from Udaipur (below), Dēvapāla is called only a Paramāra ruler without mention of his capital.
Undapura unidentified by the editor; Kielhorn states it is probably mentioned also in the Udayapur inscription.
Kielhorn's reading of the Udayapur inscription gives [Uda?]pura (No. 28, unpublished).

items.note: Genealogy in Dēvapāla's Māndhātā grant: Bhōja, Udayāditya, Naravarman, Yaśōvarman, Ajayavarman, Vindhyavarman, Subhaṭavarman, Arjunavarman; then Dēvapāla, son of Harischandra.
Dēvapāla's relationship with Arjunavarman is not stated; Arjunavarman probably died without male heir and Dēvapāla may have united both houses at Dhārā.
